---
title: "A decimal comma gives NA"
ref: NUM-11
categories: [Numbers]
impact: silencieux
extrait: 'as.numeric("1,5")'
reponse: 'NA'
attendu: "`1.5`"
versions: "All"
source: "General R knowledge"
---

::: {.piege}
```{r}
price <- c("1,5", "2", "3,25")
as.numeric(price)
mean(as.numeric(price), na.rm = TRUE)
```
:::

## Why

R only accepts the dot as decimal separator, whatever the system language. A string containing a comma is not a number to R: it becomes `NA`, with a mere warning.

Whole values, on the other hand, go through. The result therefore looks plausible: here the "mean" is 2, computed on the only value without a comma.

## The fix

Replace the comma before converting, or read the file with `read.csv2()`, which expects the decimal comma used in France and much of Europe.

::: {.piege}
```{r}
as.numeric(sub(",", ".", x = price, fixed = TRUE))
read.csv2(text = "price\n1,5\n2\n3,25")
```
:::
